paragraphs: Rav Acha bar Adda, Chagigah 19b. In Rav Hamnuna’s name in Rav’s name, Sukkah 21b; Eruvin 77b. Avodah Zarah 19b has Rav Acha bar Abba in Rav Hamnuna’s name in Rav’s name. He was Rav Pappa’s father and heard from Rabbi. “Heard from Rabbi” is an error, since Rav Pappa said his father Rav Acha b.A. heard from Rav (see there). Rabbi Acha son of Rava spoke to Rav Ashi, who replied, “Did you not hear Rav Acha bar Adda in Rav Hamnuna’s name in Rav’s name?” On arriving he said, “In the West,” etc., Kiddushin 30a; Nedarim 38a. In Rabbi Yehudah’s name, beginning of Chelek 90b; Rabbi Yitzchak’s name, Shabbat 17b; Avodah Zarah 36b; Ulla’s name, Bava Metzia 117b. Rava permitted him, Sukkah 26a. He was very old, his hands trembling with age; someone forged his signature while resting his own hands on a rope, Bava Batra 167a. Rav Acha bar Rav Adda spoke to Rav Ashi, Bava Metzia 8a. This requires examination: Yuchasin says he was very old in Rava’s time, as the forged-signature account brought before Rava implies. How then could he speak to Rav Ashi, born when Rava died? It must be the early Rav Ashi. Yuchasin’s “Rabbi Acha b.A. said in Rav’s name” is an error. Rabbi Yaakov bar Acha bar Idi.
